Best time to buy

What the studies say, and what it means this winter.

RedfinAugust. More listings, and sellers start offering concessions.
Realtor.comLate September to early October in most big metros.
ZillowSpring costs the most. Late-May listings sell fastest.
Late fallEarly November to mid-December is best in some metros (Redfin).
Now to JanuaryOff-peak: fewer homes, less competition, more motivated sellers.
Where to negotiateCentral and Northern NJ this winter. Pennsylvania has little room any time of year.
School yearTo move by August, sign in winter and close in summer.

How this list was built

What is in it, what is not, and where it comes from.

ListingsRedfin active listings. Every home also has a Zillow lookup link.
Filters$650,000 to $1,200,000, 3+ bedrooms, any build year, six regions.
SchoolsAssigned public schools average 7 or better on GreatSchools. No schools shown, left out.
New buildsBuilt 2025 or later is tagged New build and may not be finished.
Missing homesRedfin's feed leaves some out under MLS rules.
DistancesStraight-line miles from the map pin, not drive or train time.
Tax and insuranceFrom the listing. Where it has none, or a new build's bill covers only the land, the region's typical rate, marked estimated.

How approval works

What a lender checks, from pre-approval to closing.

The stepsPre-approval to clear to close
Pre-approvalThe lender reviews the file and writes a letter with the maximum loan. Sellers expect it with an offer.
PapersTwo years of W-2s and returns, 30 days of pay stubs, two months of bank statements, photo ID.
UnderwritingStarts at contract. The appraisal and title search are ordered.
Clear to closeOne last check before closing. Keep finances frozen until then.
IncomeWhat counts and how
Gross payIncome before taxes.
SalaryCounts once the job is verified, often by a call near closing.
Bonus or commissionUsually needs two years of history, then averaged.
Who countsOnly the people on the loan.
New job or a gapExpect questions and a letter.
Debt-to-incomeThe ratio that sets the top price
The mathNew house payment plus other monthly debts, divided by gross monthly income.
House paymentPrincipal, interest, tax, insurance, mortgage insurance, HOA.
Other debtsCar loans, student loans, minimum card payments. Not rent or utilities.
The limitThis page uses 45% conventional and 50% FHA. Both can be changed.
Down payment and cash20% down, closing costs, reserves
20% downNo mortgage insurance on a conventional loan.
Closing costsSeparate cash, set by the percent in the calculator.
ReservesLenders may want a few months of payments left in savings.
AppraisalThe house must appraise at the price. A low appraisal means covering the gap.
Bank statementsWhat they read, what to do, what to avoid
How far backTwo months, every page, for each account that funds the purchase.
Seasoned moneyIn the account 60 days: no explanation needed.
New moneyAny deposit that isn't a paycheck needs a paper trail.
DoPaychecks into the same account. Gift letters for gifts. Keep sale confirmations and every page.
AvoidCash deposits, overdrafts, large Venmo or Zelle transfers, crypto and gambling charges, new payment plans.
Loan typesConventional, FHA, jumbo
Conventional3% to 5% down at the low end. Mortgage insurance until 20% equity.
FHA3.5% down. Insurance lasts the life of the loan with under 10% down. County loan limits apply.
JumboA loan above the conforming limit. This page assumes 20% down. Expect bigger reserves.
What lenders look forIncome, cash, the house
IncomeSteady, documented, under the debt-to-income limit.
CashDown payment, closing costs and reserves, all traceable.
The houseAppraises at the price and meets the loan's condition rules.
Nothing newA new debt or job change is the usual reason a deal stalls.
Where to compare ratesExamples only, not endorsements
Credit unionsOften low fees. PenFed, Navy Federal, or a local PA or NJ credit union.
Your own bankAsk about a discount for existing accounts.
Online lendersRocket Mortgage, Better, loanDepot.
BrokersOne application, many lenders. Ask what they charge.
Checking a quoteFreddie Mac's weekly average, Bankrate, NerdWallet, the CFPB rate tool.
Comparing3 to 5 written Loan Estimates on the same day, same points, same rate lock.
State programsNJHMFA in New Jersey and PHFA in Pennsylvania. Ask about income limits.
Get ready nowPapers and the down payment
PapersTwo years of W-2s and returns, recent pay stubs, two months of statements.
Down paymentPark it in one account for at least two months.
DebtsAdd up real monthly debts, including a planned car payment.
Stop until closingWhat stalls a deal
New cards or loansStore cards and furniture financing included.
A car loanRaises debt-to-income and lowers the top price.
Job or pay changesTell the lender first.
Big transfersLeave the money where it is.
Co-signingFor anyone.

How the numbers work

Estimates, not quotes.

RateStarts at the Freddie Mac average, 7.18%. Change it in the calculator.
Under 20% downAdds 0.125 to the rate. Under 10% down adds 0.25.
Mortgage insuranceConventional under 20% down: 0.40% to 1.00% of the loan a year, by down payment.
FHARate starts 0.25 lower. 3.5% down, 1.75% up front, then 0.50% to 0.75% a year.
JumboAbove the conforming limit: needs 20% down and adds 0.15 to the rate.
Conforming limits$832,750 baseline. $1,249,125 in the NYC-area NJ and NY counties.
FHA limits$630,200 in Pennsylvania and Southern NJ. $1,249,125 in the NYC-area counties.
Ask every lenderHow they count bonus pay, and a written estimate. Rates move daily.
